title: Total-fraction localization decomposes into minimal-prime fibres
statement: Let R be a reduced Noetherian commutative ring in universe u [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], A a commutative R-algebra in universe max(u,v), and S the nonzerodivisors of R. There exist n, an enumeration q: Fin n ≃ {p ∈ Spec R | p is minimal}, a ring isomorphism e: S⁻¹R ≃ ∏_i κ(q_i), and a ring isomorphism f: S⁻¹A ≃ ∏_i (κ(q_i) ⊗_R A), such that f(algebraMap(r))_i = algebraMap(e(r)_i) for every r in S⁻¹R and i in Fin n. Residue fields and fibres are those of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], and localizations are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. No Noetherianity, reducedness, nontriviality or regularity is assumed for A.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 02LX; Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07F5 (lemma-reduce-to-field), third paragraph of the proof

proof.text: Apply reduced_noetherian_total_ring_fractions to obtain n and q, bijective canonical maps from each prime localization to its residue field, and unique compatible maps φ_i from the total fraction ring to the prime localizations. Choose these uniquely determined φ_i within the theorem proof. RingHom.pi φ is bijective by the decomposition theorem, and its componentwise restriction identity makes it an R-algebra homomorphism. AlgEquiv.ofBijective, followed by AlgEquiv.piCongrRight of the bijective residue-field maps, gives an R-algebra isomorphism e from the total fraction ring to the product of residue fields.

Mathlib Localization.tensorRightAlgEquiv identifies S⁻¹A with (S⁻¹R) ⊗_R A. Apply tensor symmetry, tensor congruence with e, Algebra.TensorProduct.piRight for the finite product, then tensor symmetry in each factor. Their composite is the required ring isomorphism f to the product of fibres. This is the base-change property of localization followed by Mathlib finite-product tensor distribution.

The inverse localization equivalence sends the scalar r to r ⊗ 1. The next maps send it successively to 1 ⊗ r, 1 ⊗ e(r), the tuple of 1 ⊗ e(r)_i, and finally e(r)_i ⊗ 1. This is exactly the scalar map into each fibre. Tensor-product simp lemmas prove the compatibility. The same construction allows n=0, so the zero ring causes no exception.

mathlib_searches.query: A filtered colimit of smooth algebras is preserved under isomorphism of the base ring and under finite products
The total quotient ring localization of an algebra over a reduced Noetherian ring is the product of its fibres at the minimal primes, compatibly with the product of residue fields of the base
mathlib_searches.results: PrimeSpectrum.piLocalizationToMaximalEquiv, PrimeSpectrum.piLocalizationToMaximal_bijective, MaximalSpectrum.toPiLocalizationEquiv, Localization.AtPrime.mapPiEvalRingHom_bijective, and related spectrum localization definitions. No exact match for the compatible two-ring decomposition.

Mathlib.CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.Ind provides transport of colimit presentations and closure under isomorphisms. Mathlib.RingTheory.TensorProduct.Pi provides Algebra.TensorProduct.piRight. Mathlib has AlgCat.restrictScalarsEquivalenceOfRingEquiv, but no corresponding CommAlgCat equivalence in Basic. The project has the proved binary Algebra.ind_smooth_prod; no combined finite-product/base-transport statement.

lean.statement:
theorem total_fraction_fiber_decomposition
    (R : Type u) (A : Type (max u v)) [CommRing R] [CommRing A] [Algebra R A]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsReduced R] :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (q : Fin n ≃ {p : PrimeSpectrum R // p.asIdeal ∈ minimalPrimes R})
      (e : Localization R⁰ ≃+* ∀ i, (q i).val.asIdeal.ResidueField)
      (f : Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A R⁰) ≃+*
        ∀ i, (q i).val.asIdeal.Fiber A),
      ∀ r i, f (algebraMap (Localization R⁰)
          (Localization (Algebra.algebraMapSubmonoid A R⁰)) r) i =
        algebraMap ((q i).val.asIdeal.ResidueField) ((q i).val.asIdeal.Fiber A) (e r i)
